method: initialize + tools/list (anonymous, no tool called; roadmap#992)

tools.name: package_search_grep
tools.description:
## Description
Executes a grep over the source code of a public package. This tool is useful for deterministically finding code in a package using regex. 
Use this tool before implementing solutions that use external packages.
The regex pattern should be restrictive enough to only match code you're looking for, to limit overfetching.

Required Args: "registry", "package_name", "pattern"
Optional Args: "version", "language", "filename_sha256", "a", "b", "c", "head_limit", "output_mode"

Best for: Deterministic code search, finding specific code patterns, or exploring code structure.

a.description: The number of lines after a grep match to include

b.description: The number of lines before a grep match to include

c.description: The number of lines before and after a grep match to include

filename_sha256.description: The sha256 hash of the file to filter for"

head_limit.description:
Limits number of results returned. 
If the number of results returned is less than the head limit, all results have been returned.

languages.description:
The languages to filter for. If not provided, all languages will be searched.
    Valid options: "Rust", "Go", "Python", "JavaScript", "JSX", "TypeScript", "TSX", "HTML", "Markdown", "YAML", "Bash", "SQL", "JSON", "Text", "Dockerfile", "HCL", "Protobuf", "Make", "Toml", "Jupyter Notebook"

output_mode.description:
Controls the shape of the grep output.
Accepted values:
- "content" (default): return content snippets with line ranges
- "files_with_matches": return unique files (path and sha256) that match
- "count": return files with the count of matches per file

package_name.description:
The name of the requested package. Pass the name as it appears in the package manager. 
For Go packages, use the GitHub organization and repository name in the format {org}/{repo}, if unsure check the GitHub URL for the package and use {org}/{repo} from that URL.

pattern.description:
The regex pattern for exact text matching in the codebase. Must be a valid regex.
    Example: "func\\s+(get_repository|getRepository)\\s*\\(.*?\\)\\s*\\{"

registry_name.description: The name of the registry containing the requested package. Must be one of: "crates_io", "golang_proxy", "npm", or "py_pi".

version.description:
Optionally, the specific version of the package whose source code to search.  
If provided, must be in semver format: {major}.{minor}.{patch}. 
Otherwise, the latest indexed version of the package available will be used.

tools.name: package_search_hybrid
tools.description:
## Description
Searches package source code using semantic understanding AND optionally regex patterns.
This allows for hybrid search, allowing for prefiltering with regex, and semantic ranking.

Required Args: "registry", "package_name", "semantic_queries"

Optional Args: "version", "filename_sha256", "pattern", "language"

Best for: Understanding how packages implement specific features, finding usage patterns, or exploring code structure.

filename_sha256.description: The sha256 hash of the file to filter for"

languages.description:
The languages to filter for. If not provided, all languages will be searched.
    Valid options: "Rust", "Go", "Python", "JavaScript", "JSX", "TypeScript", "TSX", "HTML", "Markdown", "YAML", "Bash", "SQL", "JSON", "Text", "Dockerfile", "HCL", "Protobuf", "Make", "Toml", "Jupyter Notebook"

tools.name: package_search_read_file
tools.description:
## Description
Reads exact lines from a source file of a public package. Useful for fetching specific code regions by line range.

Required Args: "registry", "package_name", "filename_sha256", "start_line", "end_line"
Optional Args: "version"

Best for: Inspecting exact code snippets when you already know the file and line numbers. Max 200 lines.
